newsitem.title: CANADA: Unharvested Canadian acres seen StatsCan wildcard.
newsitem.headline: Unharvested Canadian acres seen StatsCan wildcard.

text.p: A significant proportion of unharvested acres in Canada's western Prairies was seen as the wildcard in what is usually an unsurprising December Statistics Canada crop production report, analysts said.

"I don't know how StatsCan's going to account for the stuff still in the fields. Will it be counted as production yet to be harvested, as abandonment or will they revise their numbers in the spring?" Continental Grain Co (Canada) Ltd analyst Greg Kostal said.
Statistics Canada will release its latest crop production estimates at 0730 CST/1330 GMT Thursday.
Four percent of Prairie fields had yet to be combined after a cold, wet harvest, Agriculture Canada said.
About 950,000 acres seeded to the six major grains and oilseeds were not harvested in Saskatchewan, representing potential production of 760,000 tonnes, Saskatchewan Agriculture said.
Half to three-quarters of a tonne an acre could be lost to winter damage and weight loss, Saskatchewan Agriculture said.
Alberta had yet to harvest 1.09 million acres, three quarters in the Peace River Valley, Alberta Agriculture said.
All wheat output across Canada was seen between 29.859 million tonnes and 30.359 million tonnes, analysts said.
Statistics Canada in its October 8 estimate pegged all wheat at 29.859 million tonnes.
"If that all-wheat number breaks 30 (million tonnes) it could have serious ramifications for Winnipeg's feed wheat market," Bank of Nova Scotia brokerage unit Scotia McLeod analyst Rob Gigiel said.
Such a number would be among other factors weighing on wheat prices, sources said.
The Canadian Wheat Board last week revised its world feed wheat price forecast down C$11 a tonne on better world wheat production prospects.
The revision knocked Winnipeg Commodity Exchange December feed wheat futures C$6.50 a tonne lower to C$166 Tuesday from C$172.50 on Thursday, WCE traders said.

Analysts estimated barley output ahead of the StatsCan report at between 15.992 million and 16.192 million tonnes. The estimates were steady to above StatsCan's last barley estimate in October for 15.992 million tonnes.

Cold, wet harvest conditions were expected to reduce canola yields with production seen between 4.929 million and 4.85 million tonnes, analysts said. The estimates were below StatsCan's October canola estimate of 4.979 million tonnes.

Analysts, however, were at odds over flax yields since that oilseed survives frost better than canola and overwinters better, as well. Analysts' output estimates ranged between 900,000 and 834,000 tonnes.
StatsCan's flax estimate in October was 859,000 tonnes.
